rationale: The existing quote decoder is already checked against every valid non-ASCII scalar and all 32768 non-ASCII-leading two-byte inputs. Version normalization needs the same classification. Reuse that production decoder with explicit at-most-three continuation operations, preserving source overlong/surrogate/range checks, and retain each caller output policy. Make private quote hex output explicitly bounded by the source maximum eight digits. Both changes preserve the full public input domain.
roi: Two real consumers otherwise require separate UTF-8 validity reasoning and validation. Retained Kani traces show the generic quote continuation loops unrolling to the global bound, so explicit source-defined finite widths remove an observed expansion cost without substituting a test implementation. Stop at these two consumers; no general string/runtime/proof framework.
